props.title: The Entity

sections.content: The Entity stands as one of horror cinema's most unsettling supernatural assault films, based on the alleged true story of Carla Moran. Barbara Hershey's raw performance grounds this disturbing tale of invisible rape and institutional skepticism. Unlike conventional ghost stories like The Amityville Horror (1979) or Poltergeist (1982), director Sidney J. Furie takes a clinical approach, setting much of the action in sterile labs and psychiatric offices. This tension between scientific rationality and supernatural horror creates a unique psychological dread that influenced later films like Nightmare on Elm Street (1984) and Paranormal Activity (2007).

sections.content: The film's treatment of institutional gaslighting and female trauma resonates strongly with other horror classics like Rosemary's Baby (1968) and Repulsion (1965). The Entity's focus on a working-class single mother adds social commentary about vulnerability and power structures. Modern films like The Babadook (2014) and Midsommar (2019) follow this tradition of using horror to explore trauma and institutional dismissal of women's experiences. SUBHEAD: Scientific Horror and Physical Manifestation

The film's unique approach to documenting supernatural phenomena through scientific methodology sets it apart from contemporary possession films like The Exorcist (1973). The climactic attempt to trap the entity using liquid helium and strobe photography creates a fascinating collision between empirical science and supernatural horror. This influenced later scientific approaches to ghostly phenomena in films like Ghostbusters (1984) and The Conjuring (2013), where technology and paranormal investigation intersect.
